title: "Use Cases"
format: html
---

GeoCroissant addresses common integration patterns in geospatial machine learning. The sections below outline nine use cases, their relevant properties, and practical implementation examples.

---

## Use Case 1: Space Weather Datasets

Heliophysics and space weather datasets (such as solar imagery from NASA's SDO and GOES satellites) follow the SPASE standard. These datasets use observatories, instruments, and wavelength channels rather than geographic bounding boxes and projections.

GeoCroissant provides two composite structures for this domain:

| Property | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `geocr:multiWavelengthConfiguration` | Lists wavelength channels (e.g. via `geocr:channelList`) |
| `geocr:solarInstrumentCharacteristics` | Records observatory and instrument identifiers |

```json
{
  "geocr:multiWavelengthConfiguration": {
    "@type": "geocr:MultiWavelengthConfiguration",
    "geocr:channelList": ["171Å", "193Å"]
  },
  "geocr:solarInstrumentCharacteristics": {
    "@type": "geocr:SolarInstrumentCharacteristics",
    "geocr:observatory": "SDO",
    "geocr:instrument": "AIA"
  }
}
```

Recipe: [Space Weather & Heliophysics (SDO)](Solar Dynamics Observatory GeoCroissant/SDO GeoCroissant.ipynb).

## Use Case 2: Interoperability with Other Standards

Geospatial workflows frequently require translating metadata between catalog systems. GeoCroissant fields map directly to equivalent concepts in STAC and GeoDCAT:

| STAC Field | GeoCroissant Field | External Vocabulary |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `@id` | — |
| `title` | `name` | `dcat:title` |
| `description` | `description` | `dcat:description` |
| `bbox` | — | `sc:spatialCoverage` / `dcat:bbox` |
| `geometry` | — | `geosparql:hasGeometry` |
| `assets` | `distribution` | `dcat:distribution` |
| `proj:epsg` | `geocr:coordinateReferenceSystem` | `proj:epsg` |
| `gsd` | `geocr:spatialResolution` | `stac:gsd` |
| `eo:bands` | `geocr:bandConfiguration`, `geocr:spectralBandMetadata` | STAC EO extension |

Recipes: [GeoCroissant to STAC](GeoCroissant to STAC/conversion-stac-notebook.ipynb) and [GeoCroissant to GeoDCAT](GeoCroissant to GeoDCAT/conversion-geodcat-notebook.ipynb).

## Use Case 3: Programmatic Metadata Access

When dataset metadata is hosted in an active catalog or registry, `geocr:recordEndpoint` points clients to the query endpoint. This aligns with the OGC API - Records specification.

Clients can query records with spatial and temporal filters:

```http
GET /api/records?bbox=-125,24,-66,49
GET /api/records?datetime=2018-01-01/2021-12-31
```

The resulting GeoJSON FeatureCollection can be parsed directly by spatial clients:

```json
{
  "geocr:recordEndpoint": "https://example.org/api/records",
  "recordSet": [{
    "@type": "cr:RecordSet",
    "@id": "records_recordset",
    "field": [
      { "@type": "cr:Field", "name": "recordId", "dataType": "sc:Text" },
      { "@type": "cr:Field", "name": "spatialCoverage", "dataType": "sc:Place" },
      { "@type": "cr:Field", "name": "temporalCoverage", "dataType": "sc:Text" },
      { "@type": "cr:Field", "name": "geocr:spatialResolution", "dataType": "sc:QuantitativeValue" },
      { "@type": "cr:Field", "name": "geocr:spatialIndex", "dataType": "sc:Text" }
    ]
  }]
}
```

## Use Case 4: Search and Discovery via GeoSPARQL

GeoCroissant expresses geometries using GeoSPARQL predicates, enabling spatial queries over RDF datasets in triplestores such as GraphDB. The `geocr:spatialIndex` property provides fast index-based filtering before polygon comparisons.

See [Appendix B](spec-appendix.qmd#appendix-b-geosparql-query-examples) for query examples.

## Use Case 5: ML Pipeline Ingestion

GeoCroissant metadata loads directly into PyTorch, TensorFlow, and JAX datasets without custom format glue code.

```python
import mlcroissant as mlc
import torch
from torch.utils.data import Dataset, DataLoader
import rasterio
import numpy as np
from pathlib import Path

# Load dataset metadata
dataset = mlc.Dataset("Introduction to Geocroissant/hls_burn_scars.json")
metadata = dataset.metadata

class HLSDataset(Dataset):
    def __init__(self, records):
        self.records = records

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.records)

    def __getitem__(self, idx):
        rec = self.records[idx]
        with rasterio.open(rec["image"]) as src:
            image = src.read().astype(np.float32)
        with rasterio.open(rec["mask"]) as src:
            mask = src.read(1).astype(np.int64)
        return {"image": torch.from_numpy(image), "mask": torch.from_numpy(mask)}
```

Recipe: [Introduction to GeoCroissant](Introduction to Geocroissant/Introduction to Geocroissant.ipynb).

## Use Case 6: Responsible GeoAI Documentation

Responsible AI metadata documents dataset origins, known geographic omissions, and sampling rules. GeoCroissant extends the [Croissant RAI extension](http://mlcommons.org/croissant/RAI/1.0) with spatial fields:

```json
{
  "geocr:spatialBias": "Spatial coverage is concentrated over the contiguous United States; high-latitude regions and other global biomes are not represented.",
  "geocr:samplingStrategy": "512x512 pixel chips were sampled by centering windows on burn-scar polygons; cloudy scenes were removed.",
  "rai:dataCollection": "Chips generated by co-locating HLS scenes with reference burn polygons.",
  "rai:dataBiases": "Geographic bias (CONUS only) and temporal bias (2018-2021).",
  "rai:dataUseCases": ["Training", "Validation", "Testing"]
}
```

Recipe: [Responsible AI Specifications](GeoCroissant & Responsible AI (RAI) Specs/GeoCroissant (RAI) Specifications.ipynb).

## Use Case 7: Time-Series Earth Observation

Time-series models for change detection and crop monitoring require explicit chronological sequencing. GeoCroissant declares the timestamp field with `geocr:timeSeriesIndex` and observation cadence with `geocr:temporalResolution`:

```json
{
  "geocr:temporalResolution": { "@type": "QuantitativeValue", "value": 1, "unitText": "month" },
  "recordSet": [{
    "@type": "cr:RecordSet",
    "@id": "timeseries_recordset",
    "geocr:timeSeriesIndex": { "@id": "timeseries_recordset/timestamp" },
    "field": [
      {
        "@type": "cr:Field",
        "@id": "timeseries_recordset/timestamp",
        "name": "timestamp",
        "dataType": "sc:DateTime"
      },
      {
        "@type": "cr:Field",
        "@id": "timeseries_recordset/image",
        "name": "image",
        "dataType": "sc:ImageObject"
      }
    ]
  }]
}
```

Recipe: [Time-Series Support](GeoCroissant Time-Series Support/GeoCroissant Time-Series Support.ipynb).

## Use Case 8: Custom Vocabulary Terms

When an attribute already exists in an established standard (GeoSPARQL, SPASE, Dublin Core), declare the prefix in `@context` and use the term directly.

When no existing vocabulary applies, use `sc:additionalProperty` with `sc:PropertyValue`:

```json
{
  "additionalProperty": [
    {
      "@type": "PropertyValue",
      "name": "cloudCoverMedian",
      "value": { "@type": "QuantitativeValue", "value": 12.3, "unitText": "%" }
    },
    {
      "@type": "PropertyValue",
      "name": "tilingScheme",
      "value": "MGRS"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Use Case 9: Scientific Container Mappings

Scientific data containers (GeoParquet, HDF5, NetCDF) organize arrays into internal tables, groups, and chunks. GeoCroissant maps individual fields directly to container paths without requiring data duplication.

Recipes: [GeoParquet to GeoCroissant](GeoCroissant GeoParquet Support/GeoParquet to GeoCroissant.ipynb) and [Landslide4Sense HDF5 to GeoCroissant](Landslide4Sense-HDF5 GeoCroissant/Landslide4Sense-HDF5 GeoCroissant.ipynb).
